paragraphs.title: The Rebellious People, Judgment, and the Preserved Remnant

answers: A nation that was not called by his name
easy.explanation: The Lord reveals Himself to a nation that had not been called by His name.
easy.q: To whom does the Lord say, “Behold me, behold me”?

easy.explanation: The people are called rebellious and are said to walk in a way that was not good.
Like new wine in a cluster, the Lord will preserve His servants and not destroy them all.
easy.q: What will the Lord not do to His servants?

answers: Because they rebel, worship falsely, and practice impurity
Because they refuse to build houses
medium.explanation: They provoke the Lord, burn incense to false gods, and practice defiling acts.
medium.q: Why does the Lord judge the people?

answers: The Lord continually invited the people to respond
The Lord hid Himself from the people
The Lord prepared to leave the land
medium.explanation: The image expresses the Lord’s continual appeal to a rebellious people.
medium.q: What does “I have spread out my hands all the day” show?

answers: The Lord will preserve His servants
The people will abandon the mountains
medium.explanation: The good cluster represents the servants whom the Lord will spare.
medium.q: What is the point of the cluster containing a blessing?

answers: The Lord reaches out, but the people continue rebelling
The people call, but the Lord refuses to answer
The people worship truly, but the land becomes empty
challenge.explanation: God extends His hands while the people persist in their sinful ways.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast at the beginning of the passage?

answers: A preserved group will inherit the land
Everyone will be destroyed without exception
The land will remain completely uninhabited
challenge.explanation: The passage promises an inheritor from Judah and dwelling places for God’s servants.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the mention of Jacob, Judah, and the Lord’s servants?

answers: They will become places of pasture for God’s people
They will become places of burial
challenge.explanation: Sharon will be a fold for flocks and Achor a resting place for herds.
challenge.q: What does the description of Sharon and the valley of Achor indicate?

paragraphs.title: Sinners versus God’s Servants and the Reversal of Their Fates

easy.explanation: They are explicitly described as those who forsake the Lord.
They prepare a table for “that troop” and furnish a drink offering unto that number.
easy.q: For whom do they prepare a table?

easy.explanation: The servants will eat, drink, and rejoice.
easy.q: What will the Lord’s servants do?

answers: They are numbered to the sword
They are given a new vineyard
medium.explanation: Because they do not answer or hear, they face judgment and slaughter.
medium.q: What results when the people do not answer when the Lord calls?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a liquid offering connected with their false worship.
medium.q: In this context, what is a “drink offering”?

answers: Sinners hunger and thirst, while servants eat and rejoice
Sinners rejoice, while servants receive food
Sinners inherit the mountains, while servants leave them
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts hunger, thirst, and shame with eating, drinking, and rejoicing.
medium.q: How are the fates of sinners and servants reversed?

answers: The different destinies of God’s servants and the sinners
challenge.explanation: The servants sing with joy, while the sinners cry because of sorrow and vexation.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between “joy of heart” and “sorrow of heart” emphasize?

answers: A change in the servants’ identity and status
challenge.explanation: The new name marks a changed condition for the Lord’s servants.
challenge.q: What does being called “by another name” suggest?

answers: The future is blessed after the former troubles disappear from memory
The troubles remain the center of the future
challenge.explanation: The passage connects blessing in the God of truth with the former troubles being forgotten.
challenge.q: How are forgotten troubles connected with blessing?

paragraphs.title: The New Heavens and Earth and Joyful Jerusalem

answers: New heavens and a new earth
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I create new heavens and a new earth.”

answers: The former troubles and former things
easy.explanation: The former things will not be remembered or come into mind.
easy.q: What will no longer be remembered?

easy.explanation: The Lord creates Jerusalem a rejoicing and her people a joy.

answers: The voice of weeping and crying
medium.explanation: The Lord says the voice of weeping and crying will no more be heard there.
Rejoicing means gladness or great joy.
medium.q: What does “rejoicing” mean in this passage?

answers: The new creation replaces the former troubles in the people’s attention
The new creation restores the former troubles
The new earth remains without joy
medium.explanation: The former things are no longer remembered in the renewed creation.
medium.q: How are the new heavens and earth related to the former things?

answers: Their connection only to the past
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates enduring joy in what the Lord creates.
challenge.q: What does “for ever” emphasize about the gladness and rejoicing?

challenge.explanation: Jerusalem is characterized by rejoicing rather than sorrow.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in the description of Jerusalem?

answers: Jerusalem and its joy are closely connected with God’s work
The Lord is absent from Jerusalem
Jerusalem remains a place of sorrow
challenge.explanation: The Lord creates the city for joy and takes delight in it and its people.
challenge.q: What does it suggest that the Lord both creates Jerusalem and rejoices in it?

easy.explanation: The passage describes people reaching unusually advanced ages.
easy.q: How are life spans described in the renewed creation?

answers: Those who build and plant them
easy.explanation: People will inhabit the houses they build and eat the fruit of the vineyards they plant.
easy.q: Who will enjoy the houses and vineyards?

easy.explanation: The Lord says He will answer before they call.
easy.q: What will the Lord do when His people call?

answers: People will enjoy the results of their own labor
medium.explanation: No one else will take away the homes built by the workers.
medium.q: What does “they shall not build, and another inhabit” mean?

medium.explanation: The blessed seed and offspring together portray stable family life.
medium.q: What does the mention of offspring living with their parents emphasize?

answers: Their work will not be fruitless
They will work only at night
medium.explanation: Their labor will produce lasting benefit rather than being wasted.
medium.q: What does “they shall not labour in vain” mean?

answers: Security and enjoyment of the results of one’s work
challenge.explanation: People will safely enjoy their homes, crops, and the work of their hands.
challenge.q: What common idea links houses, vineyards, and labor?

answers: The speed and readiness of God’s response
challenge.explanation: God’s answer comes even before the people finish calling.
challenge.q: What does “before they call, I will answer” emphasize?

answers: They allow people time to enjoy family, homes, vineyards, and labor
They describe a life of warfare
challenge.explanation: Long life complements the promised stability of family and fruitful work.
challenge.q: How do long lives support the passage’s picture of security?

easy.explanation: The wolf and the lamb will feed together.
The lion will eat straw like the bullock.
The verse says that dust shall be the serpent’s meat.
easy.q: What will be the serpent’s meat?

answers: They live without hurting one another
medium.explanation: The animals are described peacefully, and nothing will hurt or destroy.
medium.q: What changes in the relationship among the animals?

medium.explanation: Here “feed” means to graze or eat in the pasture.
medium.q: What does “feed” mean in “the wolf and the lamb shall feed together”?

answers: It eats straw instead of preying on other animals
medium.explanation: The lion’s harmless diet shows the transformation of the animal world.
medium.q: How does the lion fit the picture of peace?

answers: A peaceful creation without harm or destruction
The abandonment of the holy mountain
challenge.explanation: The changed animals represent a world in which nothing hurts or destroys.
challenge.q: What does the change in the animals symbolize?

answers: It is harmless and eats dust
challenge.explanation: The serpent’s diet is given without any description of harm or attack.
challenge.q: What role does the serpent have in the closing picture?

answers: It shows that the promised peace extends throughout the sacred place
It limits peace to one small animal group
challenge.explanation: The phrase broadens the promise to the whole holy mountain.
challenge.q: Why is it important that peace covers “all my holy mountain”?
